To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the spatial representation of the foot position in the spinal cord is not based on joint angles, but on limb geometry.
the spatial tuning in 33/70 (47%) of the DSCT neurons is not affected by the joint constraints and that 27/70 (39%) of these neurons are significantly affected by limb geometric changes.
33/70 (47%) of the DSCT neurons we recorded encoded limb endpoint information in an axis-based reference frame.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the representation of proprioceptive information in spinal neurons and with the neural mechanisms that allow the brain to use this information to control the movement of the limbs.
the representation of limb posture in the spinal cord and its relationship with the representation of the same information in the cerebellum.
the neural mechanisms that allow the CNS to represent the position of a body part.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the activity of 33/70 neurons (47%) encoded foot position in the coordinates of a limb-based reference frame, and that 37/70 (53%) neurons did not encode foot position consistently.

53% of the DSCT neurons represent foot position independently of joint angles, whereas 14% represent one or more individual joint angles, and 33% represent neither foot position nor individual joint angles.
the activity of the majority of DSCT cells (70%) represents a foot position parameter, and that of 14% of cells represents one or more specific joints.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DSCT represents limb position and movement in a reference frame that is limb-based rather than a joint-based reference frame.
a substantial proportion of DSCT neurons represent foot position in the coordinates of a limb-based reference frame.
the majority (47/70 = 67%) of DSCT neurons represent foot position in the limb coordinates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the representation of foot position in spinal cord second-order sensory neurons is not dependent on specific joint angles.

the activity of a large fraction of DSCT neurons is not simply determined by the activity of specific muscle spindles, but rather represents a limb-based representation of foot position that can be elaborated in spite of changes in limb geometry.
a significant number of spinal neurons encode proprioceptive information about foot position in a limb-based reference frame.
